title: No Wrapped Ether
brief: Compliance says the treasury must never hold WETH. The Safe runs on a permissive catch-all, so the team denied deposit on WETH. The auditors still found WETH in the Safe. Stop all wrapping, and keep paying Dave in ETH and Erin in USDC.

rules.note: Allows every CALL without its own rule

tests.label: Send 1 ETH to WETH with no calldata
Send 1 ETH to WETH calling a made-up function
Send 1 ETH to WETH calling another made-up function

hints: WETH wraps any ETH it receives, whatever the calldata says. Most of those calls never reach the deposit rule.
You cannot block every function WETH does not have. Ask instead what the Safe should be allowed to do.
Drop the catch-all. Give plain ETH to Dave and USDC to Erin rules of their own.
explain: WETH wraps ETH for empty calldata and for any function it does not know. Those calls miss the deny rule and land on the catch-all. A blocklist cannot win against a fallback, but an allowlist can: with no permissive catch-all, every call to WETH is denied by default.
